holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found no compelling reasons justified the statutory restriction on the applicant's right of access to a lawyer during police custody and that the use of statements obtained without legal assistance irretrievably prejudiced the fairness of the proceedings.

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court concluded that the absence of good reasons for non-attendance of witnesses and the use of their statements without sufficient counterbalancing procedural safeguards irretrievably undermined the fairness of the criminal proceedings.

holdings.text: Holds (a) that the respondent State is to pay the applicant, within three months from the date on which the judgment becomes final in accordance with Article 44 § 2 of the Convention, EUR 1,500 (one thousand and five hundred euros), plus any tax that may be chargeable, in respect of non-pecuniary damage, to be converted into the currency of the respondent State, at the rate applicable at the date of settlement; (b) that from the expiry of the above-mentioned three months until settlement simple interest shall be payable on the above amount at a rate equal to the marginal lending rate of the European Central Bank during the default period plus three percentage points;
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court awarded just satisfaction for non-pecuniary damage due to the exceptional circumstances including the Government's unilateral declaration and domestic courts' failure to reopen proceedings.

holdings.text: Dismisses the remainder of the applicant’s claim for just satisfaction.
